h1: Holiday Inn Express Bangkok Soi Soonvijai — the 4-star hotel two minutes from Bangkok Hospital, with free breakfast every day
intro: If you or someone in your family needs treatment at Bangkok Hospital (BDMS) on New Petchaburi Road, the closest and most reliable place to stay in the area is Holiday Inn Express Bangkok Soi Soonvijai — just ~140 metres from the hospital entrance, a straight two-minute walk · what makes people choose this place isn't only the distance; it's the reassurance of an IHG chain at a sensible price — a free breakfast buffet every morning, free Wi-Fi, free parking and a free shuttle to MRT Phetchaburi or ARL Makkasan station · for anyone making multiple trips to the hospital each day, these small conveniences matter far more than they might look on paper · 190 rooms, open since 2017, from approx. THB 1,600–2,200/night · this review is compiled from real guest feedback on Booking.com, Agoda and TripAdvisor.

body.html: The big picture — who is this hotel for? — Holiday Inn Express Bangkok Soi Soonvijai is a 4-star IHG hotel that has positioned itself squarely for medical guests: people receiving treatment at Bangkok Hospital (BDMS), families visiting patients, or anyone with a health check-up scheduled on New Petchaburi Road · in practice, it isn't the first choice for a traveller whose main goal is exploring Bangkok's shopping and nightlife districts, because Soi Soonvijai is a quiet residential–commercial soi without any particular tourist draw of its own · but for families accompanying a patient, anyone recovering post-treatment, or business travellers with meetings in the Rama 9 / Huai Khwang corridor, this is the most logical base in the area · real reviews line up clearly: guests who came because of the hospital tend to rate the stay very highly — clean rooms, attentive staff, seamless hospital access · guests who came purely to visit Bangkok reported finding the location inconvenient for reaching Sukhumvit or Siam without a taxi or Grab every time.

Location and getting around — the hotel is at 19 Soi Soonvijai, New Petchaburi Road, Bangkapi, Huai Khwang, Bangkok 10310 · its single biggest advantage is its proximity to Bangkok Hospital (BDMS), which sits on the same road barely 140 metres away — step outside, turn right along the soi, and you are at the hospital entrance in roughly two minutes, with no road to cross and no Grab to wait for · for the train, the hotel is not within walking distance of any station, but it runs a free shuttle within an 8-km radius that covers MRT Phetchaburi (about 2–3 km away) and ARL Makkasan (about 1.2 km away), the Airport Rail Link station that connects directly to Suvarnabhumi Airport · MRT Phetchaburi in turn connects to the Rama 9 and Ratchada areas if you need to get into the city · the shuttle needs to be arranged at the front desk in advance, and during busy periods there can be a short wait.

"We stayed here to be close to my mother's treatment at Bangkok Hospital. Walking there in two minutes made everything so much easier. The staff were genuinely kind and kept checking in on us. Breakfast was good too — we'll definitely be back if we need to come again."

Room types and size — the hotel has 190 rooms, opened in 2017, split between a Standard Queen Room (one queen bed), a Standard Twin Room (two single beds), and an Accessible Room designed for guests with mobility needs — a particularly thoughtful option for patients who have just been discharged · every room is roughly 21 sq m, air-conditioned, with free Wi-Fi, a TV, a mini-fridge and a private bathroom with a shower · the steady praise in real reviews points to rooms being clean, well-maintained and modern-looking for the price · the equally steady caveat is that 21 sq m can feel tight for an extended stay — if you're travelling with medical equipment, luggage for a long visit, or caring for an elderly relative who needs extra space to move safely, the standard rooms may not be large enough · this is the honest trade-off against paying for a full-service hotel or a service apartment in the same area.

Breakfast and facilities — the element that sets Holiday Inn Express Soonvijai apart from comparable-price alternatives in the neighbourhood is that a full breakfast buffet is included in the room rate every day, served from 06:30 to 10:30 · this is genuinely practical for a hospital-stay base — you can eat before a 7am appointment without worrying about finding a cafe · real reviews largely praise the breakfast as varied and good-tasting; a smaller number flag that the Grab & Go option (for people rushing out early) is sometimes inconsistent, with cups that aren't set up for takeaway coffee · beyond breakfast, the standout facilities are a 24-hour gym (accessed with your room keycard, so no time restrictions) and a Zen garden — a quiet outdoor area that multiple reviews describe as a welcome stress-reliever between hospital visits · the hotel also has free parking, the free 8-km shuttle, a 24-hour front desk, a business centre and laundry service · there is no swimming pool, which is typical for a Holiday Inn Express in a business neighbourhood.

Service — the real standout — the word that appears most often in genuine reviews, across Booking.com, Agoda and Trip.com alike, is attentive · staff — particularly at the front desk and in housekeeping — are described as noticeably warm and willing to go a step further for guests who are clearly at the hotel because of a difficult medical situation · on Trip.com the service sub-score is 8.9, measurably higher than the overall score, which confirms this is a real pattern rather than a random comment · the honest caveats from real reviews: some rooms have the air conditioning locked at 20°C, which a number of elderly guests or post-operative patients found too cold — this is a practical issue worth flagging to the hotel at check-in or when booking · a smaller number of reviews mention a strong smell from the breakfast area on the floor where it is served, which was off-putting before eating · neither issue is common enough to be a dealbreaker, but both are worth knowing.

"Very clean room, staff looked after us especially well — they seemed to understand many guests were there because of the hospital, and that made a real difference. Breakfast was varied and genuinely tasty. Only wish the rooms were a bit bigger for a longer stay."

What real reviews say — the praise and the gripes — pooling Booking.com (705 reviews, 8.1/10), Agoda and Trip.com (854 reviews, 8.8/10), the picture is consistent · on the praise side: clean and modern rooms, genuinely attentive staff, a free breakfast that guests actually look forward to, unbeatable proximity to Bangkok Hospital, free parking and the free shuttle removing the stress of transport, and the overall confidence of staying in a recognised IHG property · on the caveat side: rooms are small at 21 sq m and can feel cramped for longer stays; AC in some rooms is preset to 20°C and not easily adjusted, uncomfortable for older guests; the hotel's location is inconvenient for leisure tourism — you'll need a Grab for almost anything beyond the hospital itself; and there is no pool · the cleanliness sub-score on Trip.com sits at 9.1, which is notably high and corroborates the consistent praise in text reviews.

Price and value — standard rooms run from roughly THB 1,600 to 2,200 per night including the free breakfast at normal low-season rates; during public holidays or peak periods prices can reach THB 2,500–3,000 · in US dollars that works out to roughly USD 44–65, which is mid-range for a branded 4-star Bangkok property · when you factor in free breakfast (saving perhaps THB 200–400 per person per day at equivalent nearby cafes), free parking and the free shuttle, the effective daily cost is lower than the room rate suggests · the value case is strongest for medical guests who need reliability and proximity above everything else · for guests considering a longer stay of several weeks, it is worth comparing nearby service apartments, which can offer larger rooms with kitchenettes at a similar or slightly higher nightly rate.

What to know before you book — a few practical notes that make the stay go more smoothly · first: Soi Soonvijai is a quiet soi, not a main road; the nearest convenience stores and street-food options require walking out to New Petchaburi Road · second: arrange the free shuttle in advance at the front desk — it is not an on-demand taxi, and during busy mornings you may need to queue · third: if the guest staying is elderly or sensitive to cold, mention the air-conditioning preference when booking or at check-in so the hotel can assign a room where it can be adjusted · fourth: check-in is at 3:00 PM and check-out at 12:00 PM, but the hotel will hold luggage if you need to leave for the hospital before or after those times · fifth: always book with free cancellation — medical schedules change, and having flexibility costs nothing when you book early enough.

highlights.title: 2-minute walk to Bangkok Hospital
highlights.text: Just ~140 metres from Bangkok Hospital (BDMS) on New Petchaburi Road — step outside and you are at the hospital entrance in 2 minutes, no road to cross, no Grab needed.

highlights.title: Free breakfast daily + free shuttle
highlights.text: A full breakfast buffet is included every morning 06:30–10:30, plus a free shuttle within 8 km — covering MRT Phetchaburi and ARL Makkasan for the airport rail link.

highlights.title: Reliable IHG standards
highlights.text: An internationally recognised IHG chain hotel — clean, modern rooms, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour gym, free parking and staff that real reviews consistently praise for being caring and attentive.

pros: Extremely close to Bangkok Hospital — 2-minute walk to the entrance

Close to both Bangkok Hospital and Praram 9 Hospital

honestSummary: Holiday Inn Express Bangkok Soi Soonvijai is the best-placed hotel in the area for anyone coming to Bangkok Hospital — the ~140 m, two-minute walk to the hospital entrance, combined with IHG reliability, a daily free breakfast and staff praised for being genuinely caring, gives it a clear edge · if your main purpose is sightseeing Bangkok, the location is inconvenient and you should consider somewhere closer to the BTS network.
honestChecks: If you need a larger room for an extended medical stay — the standard 21 sq m rooms can feel tight with medical equipment or two people for several weeks → compare nearby service apartments that offer larger rooms with kitchenettes at a similar price.

If the patient or an elderly guest is sensitive to cold — some rooms have AC preset to 20°C and cannot be easily adjusted → flag this when booking or at check-in so the hotel can assign a room with a flexible thermostat.

If you are coming primarily to sightsee Bangkok — Soi Soonvijai is away from Sukhumvit and Siam; you will need a Grab or taxi for virtually every attraction → consider a hotel near the BTS Skytrain instead for a leisure-focused trip.

tips.title: Walk straight to Bangkok Hospital
tips.body: Turn right out of the hotel entrance, walk 140 m along Soi Soonvijai and you are at the hospital entrance — no road to cross, no waiting for a car. The most stress-free aspect of staying here.

tips.title: Book the free shuttle in advance
tips.body: The free 8-km shuttle covers MRT Phetchaburi and ARL Makkasan — arrange it at the front desk the evening before, not on the morning you need it, to avoid waiting in a queue.

tips.title: Have breakfast before your early appointment
tips.body: The breakfast buffet opens at 06:30, which lines up perfectly with most morning hospital appointments. The dining room is less crowded right at opening; arrive early for the best selection.

tips.title: Request a warm-room option if needed
tips.body: If the guest is elderly, recovering from surgery or simply dislikes very cold rooms, mention this when booking or at check-in — some rooms have the AC set at 20°C; the hotel can usually accommodate a swap.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Holiday Inn Express Bangkok Soi Soonvijai

faq.q: How close is Holiday Inn Express Bangkok Soi Soonvijai to Bangkok Hospital?
faq.a: It is very close — approximately 140 metres from Bangkok Hospital (BDMS) on New Petchaburi Road, a straight two-minute walk to the hospital entrance with no road to cross · it is the nearest hotel to Bangkok Hospital in the immediate area.

faq.q: Is Holiday Inn Express Soonvijai near an MRT or BTS station?
faq.a: The hotel is not within walking distance of any train station, but it offers a free shuttle service within an 8-km radius · this covers MRT Phetchaburi (about 2–3 km away) and ARL Makkasan (about 1.2 km), the Airport Rail Link that runs directly to Suvarnabhumi Airport · arrange the shuttle with the front desk the evening before to avoid queues in the morning.

faq.q: Does the room rate include breakfast at Holiday Inn Express Soonvijai?
faq.a: Yes — a full breakfast buffet is included every day, served from 06:30 to 10:30 · this is one of the hotel's strongest points for medical-stay guests, as it lets you eat a proper meal before an early-morning hospital appointment · real reviews consistently rate the breakfast as varied and good-quality.

faq.q: Does Holiday Inn Express Soonvijai have a swimming pool?
faq.a: No, there is no swimming pool — which is standard for a Holiday Inn Express in a business neighbourhood · the hotel does have a 24-hour gym (access with your room keycard) and a Zen garden for outdoor relaxation · for guests staying because of Bangkok Hospital, reviews rarely mention the absence of a pool.

faq.q: Is Holiday Inn Express Soonvijai a good choice for general Bangkok sightseeing?
faq.a: It is less well-suited for a purely leisure trip, because Soi Soonvijai is away from Bangkok's main tourist corridors — Sukhumvit, Siam and the riverside · you would need a Grab or taxi for most attractions, which adds time and cost · it is an excellent choice for medical guests at Bangkok Hospital, business travellers in the Rama 9 / Huai Khwang area, and anyone flying in or out of Suvarnabhumi who wants a comfortable overnight near ARL Makkasan.

faq.q: What is the starting price at Holiday Inn Express Bangkok Soi Soonvijai?
faq.a: Prices start from roughly THB 1,600–2,200 per night including the free breakfast buffet at normal rates · during public holidays or peak season, rates can rise to THB 2,500–3,000 · always book with free cancellation — medical plans change — and compare a few platforms before confirming.
